Final Fantasy VII

Tifa Lockhart

Mobile melee with invincible feints, reliant on assists for damage

Fastest BRV 11F (Waterkick, Elbow Smash)Fastest HP 33F (Meteor Strike, Meteor Crusher)Dash 69 (Very Fast)ATK 108DEF 1111-hit HP NoHP links Yes

Standing in the meta

Tier B 22nd of 30 — 2017 tournament tier list from dissidia.wiki (half matchup values, half expert player votes).

Tifa is ranked 22nd, in tier B, on the 2017 competitive tier list. The overview calls her a low tier character, held back by her average bravery damage and her limited vertical aerial game.

Overview

Tifa is a highly mobile close-quarters fighter (fast run, very fast dash) with the unique ability to feint her attacks. Her ground game rests on medium priority projectiles and on an HP link (Waterkick into Somersault), her aerial game on moves with vertical tracking.

Her EX generation is decent and her EX Burst is among the most devastating in the game when plenty of EX gauge is left. Her damage potential with HP attacks is high thanks to a large base bravery and to the Aerith assist in particular.

On the other hand, weak average bravery damage, feints of limited utility and below-average vertical capabilities in the air hold back her overall effectiveness. The sources describe her as a low tier character.

Strengths

  • High mobility: a fast run and a very fast dash.
  • Invincible feints on most of her attacks, one of the game's rare sources of invincibility.
  • The Somersault HP link out of Waterkick, which starts assist combos anywhere.
  • Very high HP damage potential with a high base bravery and the Aerith assist (a double assist combo of more than 3000 HP).
  • An EX Burst among the most powerful in the game with a full EX gauge.
  • A solid ground game, able to compete with most conventional melee strategies.

Weaknesses

  • Weak average bravery damage (a very low base ATK), with momentum hard to establish even on hit.
  • Limited utility on the feints: the direction cannot be controlled, there is no mixup into another attack, and she is vulnerable after the teleport.
  • Below-average vertical capabilities in the air.
  • Heavy reliance on assists and Wall Rushes to convert into significant damage.
  • Trouble approaching against persistent projectiles, traps and zoning (Garland, The Emperor, Ultimecia).

EX Mode: Equipped Premium Heart! & EX Burst

The “Equipped Premium Heart!” EX Mode: Tifa gains Regen, Critical Boost and the permanently active Premium Heart effect, which increases the damage she deals the fuller the EX gauge is.

EX Burst : Final Heaven is an EX Burst with seven reels to stop on the “Yeah!” symbol (a steady rhythm of about 1 to 1.5 s between presses, or Auto EX Command Ω for 20 CP). Since its damage depends on the EX gauge remaining, it has to be used as soon as EX Mode is activated: at full gauge, it is one of the most powerful EX Bursts in the game.

Unique mechanic

Tifa can cancel most of her attacks into a feint: an invincible dash that passes through opponents, triggered by pressing Cross during the startup (e.g. Beat Rush > Cross > Beat Rush). She can then continue the previous attack or wait for the feint to end, with about a second of possible delay before being locked into recovery.

The feint extends an attack's range and makes its timing ambiguous (Rolling Blaze is the most famous example), notably by waiting for the opponent's block to expire. Tifa always moves forwards and only passes behind the opponent if she is close enough: the direction cannot be controlled, and there is no mixup into another attack after the feint.

The invincibility makes it an excellent defensive option against dodge punish attempts, but Tifa remains vulnerable after the teleport and during the recovery. Keeping assist gauge to cover that moment helps; using feints sparingly early in a match lets her gauge the opponent's reaction.

  • Feint windows: Beat Rush (before the 1st hit), Waterkick (before the 2nd hit), Moonsault Kick (before each part), Falcon's Dive, Dolphin Blow, Meteodrive and Burning Arrow (before the 1st hit), Meteor Strike (before or during the 1st hit, rechargeable after a feint), ground and aerial Rolling Blaze (during the first part), Meteor Crusher (before the impact, not rechargeable after a feint).
  • Documented counter-strategies: getting out of range by running or jumping, interrupting with fast attacks (Squall's Beat Fang, Yuna's Diamond Dust), following up with a homing attack (Cloud's Braver, Vaan's Inferno), or reacting with an assist to catch her in a pincer.

Gameplan & advanced tech

The heart of Tifa's game is on the ground: Waterkick as her main poke leading into the Somersault HP link, Beat Rush as a punish and as post-dodge defence, Rolling Blaze to threaten the nearby aerial space and punish dodges. Somersault combos with an assist deal considerable damage with a high base bravery, to the point of pushing the opponent to abandon the ground.

In the air, Elbow Smash is the reference poke for starting offence and building gauge, complemented by Moonsault Kick as a more damaging mixup and Falcon's Dive as a safe downward angle. The Blizzard spells let her keep her distance, build assist gauge and interrupt the opponent without committing to close-range mixups.

Almost all HP conversion goes through Wall Rushes and the assist: Rolling Blaze, Meteor Strike and Falcon's Dive to open, Meteor Crusher and aerial Rolling Blaze to finish. With Kuja, a doubled Falcon's Dive is her most damaging filler; with Aerith, an HP attack guarantees a Seal Evil follow-up and the double assist combo can exceed 3000 HP of damage.

The feints serve first and foremost defensively (invincibility after a ground dodge) and to reposition behind the opponent, but they have to be rationed: once read, they are interrupted with fast attacks or an assist. In a Side by Side build, the EX gauge is frozen: the EX Cores have to be picked up so as not to leave the generated EX Force to the opponent.

Character-specific tech

Waterkick option select

By mashing Square during Waterkick's active frames then dodging during the recovery of the first kick, Tifa covers both the hit (Somersault) and the whiff, which makes her hard to whiff punish on reaction.

Rolling Blaze feint extension

Feinting Rolling Blaze during the initial rush then chaining a second Rolling Blaze hugely extends its maximum range, with a vulnerability window so brief that punishing it demands precise timing.

Double assist combo (Aerith)

With two assist gauges: an HP attack with a Wall Rush, Aerith's Seal Evil, another Wall Rush during the Seal Evil, a second Aerith call then Rolling Blaze. A single combo can exceed 3000 HP of damage with a high base bravery build.

Knockback cancel (Beat Rush)

Cancelling the knockback of Beat Rush's third hit with an assist call keeps the opponent in place and makes the most of its 35 base damage; hard to execute but very rewarding, especially with the Sneak Attack extra ability.

Blizzaga hit glitch (Meteor Strike)

Blizzaga can cause a hit glitch on Meteor Strike, sending inattentive opponents into a damaging assist combo.

Moonsault Kick lock-off / knockback negation

Used with lock off, Moonsault Kick can be steered freely to build gauge safely in large arenas. An assist call at a very precise moment during the final rush also negates its knockback.

Documented solo combo routes

Three routes, all starting from Blizzaga, and nothing else: Blizzaga > Waterkick; Blizzaga (a hit close to the ground) > Meteodrive or Meteor Strike; Blizzaga (a hit close to the ground) > a dash to push the opponent out of the last hit > Meteor Strike.

Sources: pastebin.com/8FWDXjvJ

Universal techniques (blodge, dash feint, lock off, dodge punishment): see the Techniques & glitches page.

Matchups

Generally speaking, Tifa competes with characters using conventional melee strategies close to the ground. She struggles, on the other hand, to approach persistent projectiles (Garland) and traps (The Emperor); Ultimecia combines both with good zoning. Against Garland, she has no simple way around the Cyclone HP attack, but Aerith's Seal Evil BRV assist gets around it easily.

Aerial matchups can be difficult too (Sephiroth, for instance), between average pokes and a disappointing reward on hit. Tifa does not have many winning matchups, but she fights well on the ground: when she can lean on it or alternate ground and air, as against Firion, Jecht and Cecil, she is well placed to make big plays.

Match videos: Replay Theater — Tifa Lockhart matches.

Builds

Three builds are documented, all at 450 CP assuming the Equip Glitch. The first, an “all-rounder” Side by Side (Kuja assist, Seventh Heaven, a constant x2.7 booster), aims for an attack/defence balance: defensive equipment (Hero's Shield against HP Wall Rush damage), accessories geared towards gauge depletion and bravery boosts on block/dodge, a high base bravery and Assist Critical Boost to make up for her average damage. Kuja converts Wall Rushes, staggers and unfinished bravery sequences.

The second, a high base bravery Side by Side (1623 BRV, Aerith assist, x3.5 booster), maximises damage: an HP attack, Aerith's Seal Evil, then a second HP attack once base bravery has been recovered, for more than 3000 HP in a single combo. Aerith is the only competitive assist that converts a full Moonsault Kick without a wall, and the double assist combo is the build's signature. Side by Side freezes the EX gauge: the EX Cores have to be picked up.

The third, BRV Boost on Dodge (the Adamant Chains set, an x5.5 booster, 146 BRV per dodge at full tilt), is reserved for matchups where Tifa takes a lot of projectiles: it discourages Sephiroth's Shadow Flare and helps against The Emperor and Ultimecia, three matchups that remain difficult even so. The extra bravery justifies taking the risk to land an HP attack.

Assist synergies

Tifa Lockhart as an assist

As an assist, Tifa has Beat Rush (ground BRV, 21F, Chase), Falcon's Dive (air BRV, 23F, Wall Rush), Meteodrive (ground HP, 39F, Wall Rush) and Rolling Blaze (air HP, 45F, Wall Rush), all appearing on the opponent.

She is ranked Low on Muggshotter's assist tier list.

Recommended assists

  • Kuja — Conversions off pokes and Wall Rushes with heavy bravery damage, at the cost of a high risk of seeing him locked when he is used.
  • Tidus — The same conversions as Kuja with less damage, but a faster startup and a shorter aerial BRV assist animation, which makes him safer even if the opponent escapes with LV1 Assist Change.
  • Aerith — She boosts damage close to the ground with triple HP combos and reliably converts the Moonsault Kick chase; recommended for Side by Side and/or high base bravery builds.

Known limits

  • The wiki's Combos section is empty (documented: false): no detailed, quantified combo is provided, and only the indications in the move and build notes were used.
  • No external reference (the References section is empty): no attributable communityTech.
  • The overview's Strengths/Weaknesses table is empty in the data; strengths and weaknesses were deduced from the overview text, the move notes and the matchups.
  • The assist gauge gains (assistGain) are not filled in for any move.
  • Somersault's startup is unknown in the data (“?”), and the EX Burst's damage type is marked “??”.
